clue.text: President Biden finally pursuing the big picture?

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the final letter follows the big-picture word

parts.note: the macro view is the big-picture view, so this gives MACRO

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Biden

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what comes after the US president leaves office, framed as a broad overview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Biden' reads as one person, but only 'President' is the definition; Biden supplies just his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the President of France, so a head of state is a fair definition.

clue.text: Tiny island stupidly quits EU following conclusion of referendum

indicators.note: following places the scrambled letters after the single letter
the conclusion of a word is its closing letter, here from referendum
acting stupidly suggests the letters of quits EU are muddled up

explanation.surface: A small island foolishly leaves the European Union after a referendum result, a Brexit joke in miniature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges QUITSEU into USTIQUE; the M from the end of 'referendum' goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustique is a small private island in the Grenadines, a Caribbean resort for the wealthy.

clue.text: Irish family group put off dividing spoils

indicators.note: dividing means the scrambled letters split the band's name in two

parts.note: The Corrs are an Irish band made up of siblings

indicators.note: off suggests the word put is spoiled or shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish family band puts off sharing out the spoils of their success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns PUT into UPT, which goes inside CORRS between CORR and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt something is to taint or ruin it, which is what spoiling means as a verb.

clue.text: Bess's partner quietly leaving wild party

indicators.note: leaving signals that the letter for quietly departs from the partner's name

parts.note: Porgy partners Bess in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Bess's companion slips away silently from a raucous party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, unrestrained party, usually with heavy drinking or sex.

clue.text: Small Channel Islands firm — with my backing — imported heater from Africa

indicators.note: backing means the exclamation for my is read backwards

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A small Channel Islands business imports heaters from Africa with my financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns COR (British 'my!') into ROC. The scirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa into southern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The scirocco is a hot wind carried from the Sahara to Italy and the Mediterranean, warming it.

clue.text: Top officer over in DEFCON reportedly avoided rules

parts.note: CO is the commanding officer, the officer in charge

indicators.note: in places the letter for over inside the word DEFCON

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for avoided is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to duck something is to avoid it, giving DUCKED

explanation.surface: A senior officer dodges an emergency at a high military alert level, DEFCON being the US defence readiness scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside DEFCON to make DEOFCON; 'reportedly' turns DUCKED into the same-sounding DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: A code of conduct is a set of rules governing how people should behave.

clue.text: Conservative/right English landlord

parts.note: a publican is the landlord of a British pub

explanation.surface: A right-wing English pub landlord, the stereotype of a Conservative voter behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash makes 'Conservative' look like part of a list, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are the conservative party in American politics, so a Republican is a conservative.

clue.text: Young mum with expensive taste stealing a grand from coach

indicators.note: stealing means the named letters are taken away from the coach word

parts.note: a carriage is a horse-drawn or railway coach
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A young mother with costly tastes takes a thousand pounds from a coach, a nod to political funding rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrie Johnson, wife of Boris Johnson, was criticised over the lavish refurbishment of their Downing Street flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrie Johnson, a young mother, became known for an expensive flat makeover funded by a donor.

clue.text: Got rid of old American Cruz?

parts.note: Ted Cruz is a US senator from Texas

explanation.surface: A question asking whether an old American politician named Cruz was thrown out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove them from a position, so ousted means removed.

clue.text: One of Boris's progeny?

indicators.note: one of suggests a piece taken from within the phrase Boris's progeny, spanning both words

explanation.surface: A question about one of Boris Johnson's many children.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'BoriS PROGeny'; the whole clue also defines it, as Boris Johnson has several children.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child, so one of anyone's offspring is a sprog.

clue.text: Candidates for transplant dopy coming round in London hospital

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the hospital's name

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London

indicators.note: coming round, like a patient waking, suggests the letters of dopy turning into a new order

explanation.surface: A drowsy patient comes round after an operation in a London hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' rearranges DOPY into ODYP, which sits after the B of BARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs such as kidneys and hearts are parts of the body that may be transplanted.

clue.text: Anniversary gift using a third battery

indicators.note: using suggests the letters are taken and worked into something new

explanation.surface: A present for an anniversary that runs on a third battery, like a toy needing extra power.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all thirteen letters of 'a third battery'; 'battery' itself hints at a battering of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat given on someone's birthday marks the anniversary of their birth.

clue.text: Devout priest discharged debts

indicators.note: discharged means the letter for priest is sent away from the word

parts.note: pious means devout

explanation.surface: A devout priest has his debts cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' looks like it goes with 'debts' (discharged debts are paid), but it is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An IOU is a written acknowledgement of money owed, so IOUs are records of debts.

clue.text: Hence Rees-Mogg & co ring?

parts.note: the ERG is the European Research Group of Brexit-backing Tory MPs, including Jacob Rees-Mogg
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Asking whether Jacob Rees-Mogg and his allies form a ring, so a political conclusion follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERG (European Research Group) is a hard-Brexit faction of British Conservative MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, a word for drawing a logical conclusion.

clue.text: 26 billion invested in 1A's cheese?

definitions.note: 26-down is BUNG, which here means a bribe

indicators.note: invested in means the letter for billion is placed inside the cheese

parts.note: brie is a French cheese, so it belongs to 1A, the French president

explanation.surface: A billion is sunk into a French president's favourite cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 26-down is BUNG, British slang for a bribe; 1A is MACRON, so his cheese is French BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is slang for an illicit payment, the same thing as a bribe.

clue.text: Simpleton runs hotel in Scottish city commercial

indicators.note: in places the letters for runs and hotel inside the city's name

parts.note: Dundee is a city in eastern Scotland
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A fool runs a hotel in a Scottish city and makes a commercial for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunderhead is a stupid person, a dimwit or fool.

clue.text: Hunt ruthlessly admits lie

indicators.note: admits means the phrase Hunt ruthlessly lets the answer in, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: A politician named Hunt brutally confesses to lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like the definition's verb, confessing; it signals the answer sitting inside 'hUNT RUTHlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a false statement, which is what a lie is.

clue.text: Firm provided partial cover

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
if means provided, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: A company offers insurance that only partly covers you, provided conditions are met.
explanation.definitionFit: A coif is a close-fitting cap covering the top of the head, so it covers only part of it.

clue.text: Recommend eggy drink when dropping a tablet

indicators.note: when dropping means the single letter a falls out of the drink's name

parts.note: advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, brandy and sugar
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone suggests an eggy drink when taking a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one A from ADVOCAAT leaves ADVOCAT, before E. 'dropping a tablet' looks like taking a pill, but 'a' is the letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course of action is to speak in favour of it, to recommend it.

clue.text: Cons' miry, dirty, dodgy practice?

indicators.note: dirty suggests the letters are soiled and messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Muddy, dirty Tories engaged in dodgy dealings, Cons being short for Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cons' looks like the Conservatives, and their dirty practices are the theme, but it is plain anagram fodder with 'miry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronyism is favouritism shown to friends, for example in political appointments, a shady practice.

clue.text: Thought India deal almost complete

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: almost complete means the word deal is given short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A trade deal with India is nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: German theologian never to accept a new Germany

indicators.note: to accept means the word for never takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ne'er is a poetic contraction of never
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A German theologian refuses ever to accept a reunified Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Joachim Neander was a 17th-century German Reformed theologian and hymn writer, after whom the Neander valley, and so Neanderthal man, is named.
explanation.definitionFit: Joachim Neander, and also the church historian August Neander, were German theologians.

clue.text: Like the sound of lamb stuffed with Indian bread fruit

indicators.note: stuffed with means the bleat is filled with the bread

parts.note: baa is the bleating sound a lamb makes
nan (naan) is a flat Indian bread

explanation.surface: A dish of lamb stuffed with naan bread and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the sound of' hints that something is said aloud, but it simply gives the bleat BAA, which holds NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with yellow skin.

clue.text: Lazes around Spain fiddling?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of lazes are turned about into a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Someone idles about in Spain, perhaps playing the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges LAZES into SLEAZ. 'fiddling' looks like playing a violin, but here means cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaze is corrupt or dishonest conduct, such as fiddling expenses, especially in politics.

clue.text: More competent sailor holding end of rope in both hands

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: in places the final letter of rope inside the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both hands

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word rope

explanation.surface: A capable sailor grips the end of a rope with both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' only links the sailor to the rest; the E from rope's end sits inside L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, meaning having greater skill or competence.

clue.text: Tough husband taken on by harbour vessel

indicators.note: taken on by means the husband's letter is taken aboard the vessel, inside it

parts.note: a tug is a small boat that tows ships in a harbour

explanation.surface: A rugged husband gets a job on a tugboat in the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' looks like an adjective but is a noun here, a hard man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, as a noun, is a rough violent man, the same as a thug.

clue.text: Anna possibly stealing Colin's heart

indicators.note: stealing means a letter is taken away from the name Colin, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as the name Colin

explanation.walkthrough: Anna looks like a woman's name, but it was a coin of British India worth one sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian currency unit, so it is an example of a coin.

clue.text: Seal upper part of single-storey residence

parts.note: a bungalow is a house with only one storey

explanation.walkthrough: A bungalow has no upper floor, which makes 'upper part' a joke; here it is the first half of BUNGALOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a stopper for closing a hole in a barrel, so to bung is to seal.

clue.text: Lowering a cellar

parts.note: a basement is a cellar, the floor below ground

explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation or degradation, the act of bringing someone low in status.

clue.text: Taste a bit of satsuma Miss?

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'satsUMA MIss'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: Funny story involving dance and broken toe

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters of dance and toe are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An amusing tale about a dance that ended in a broken toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like it describes the toe, but it rearranges the letters of both DANCE and TOE.

clue.text: Shining silver lamé creation

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
